name: Background jobs
summary: Queue work and run it reliably with retries, backoff, and a dead-letter queue

env.name: DATABASE_URL
env.description: Branch connection string. Injected automatically by Neon.

env.name: NEON_BLOCKS_TRIGGER_SECRET
env.description: Shared secret appended to trigger paths as ?secret=. Neon does not sign trigger delivery, so this is the only way to authenticate rather than merely recognise an event.

env.name: QUEUE_BATCH_SIZE
env.description: Jobs claimed per invocation. Raise for throughput, lower to bound per-invocation cost.

env.name: QUEUE_LEASE_SECONDS
env.description: How long a claimed job may run before another worker may steal it. Must exceed your slowest handler.

env.name: QUEUE_BUDGET_MS
env.description: Stop claiming new work after this long so the invocation ends cleanly. Billing runs until the handler returns.

env.name: QUEUE_RETENTION_DAYS
env.description: How long succeeded jobs and delivered events are kept before the sweeper purges them.

env.name: QUEUE_CONCURRENCY
env.description: Per-type concurrency caps as JSON, e.g. {"rag.embed":4}. Guards against a firehose consuming all capacity.

triggers.description: Drain the outbox and run due jobs. Every minute is the practical floor for cron-driven reactivity.
Reclaim expired leases, purge old succeeded jobs, report DLQ depth. Off-peak and off the hour.

operations.title: POST /work
operations.description: cron, every minute — drain the outbox, then run due jobs

operations.title: POST /sweep
operations.description: cron, daily — reclaim leases, purge, report DLQ depth

operations.title: POST /enqueue
operations.description: HTTP — enqueue a job from application code

operations.title: POST /publish
operations.description: HTTP — publish an event to the outbox

operations.title: POST /replay
operations.description: HTTP — move dead jobs back to pending after a fix
